records.summary: User-requested check of three subsystems (power graph incl. supply shortage, beaver pathfinding, area-effect buildings). Inclusive Harmony timing of every non-accessor method of 33 classes (src/T3MPTestDriver/SubsystemProfiler.cs, -t3mpTestSubsystemProfile) on installed v1.2.2 (CAA2B508), n10c x50; hooks add about 0.15 us per timed call, nested rows overlap, ticks/s fell to 14.1 during the run.

per_window.NeedManager.Tick: 4880 ms inclusive, 497k calls; UpdateNeed 16.8M calls (34 needs per character per tick), CheckNewState 17.4M. Component-level profile without inner hooks: 2.2 ms/tick, about 4-5% of the 45 ms tick.
per_window.pathfinding: PathfindingService.FindPathUncached 1695 ms / 94k calls (313 per tick) plus the 5-argument overload 630 ms / 11k; FlowFieldPathFinder.FindPathInFlowField 965 ms / 820k; FindRoadPathIfCachedAndFillIfNeeded 900 ms / 162k; NavigationService.FindTerrainPath 685 ms / 591k (1971 per tick: behavior distance/reachability queries against cached flow fields); TransformPathIntoPathCorners 512 ms / 44k (11.5 us per path, 23 nodes each, IPathTransformer chain per node); RoadAStarPathfinder.FillFlowFieldWithPath 264 ms / 57k; TerrainAStarPathfinder 103 ms / 7k. A* uses BinaryHeap with lazy deletion; no algorithmic pitfall found. Real share about 7% of the tick, spread over cached lookups and corner transforms.
per_window.ranged_effects: RangedEffectSubject.Tick 1237 ms / 497k (per character per tick), ToContinuousEffect 246 ms / 627k, GetEfficiency 159 ms / 627k, NeedManager.ApplyEffect 531 ms / 721k, GetAffectingEffects 280 ms. Coverage (RangedEffectService.SetApplier, RangedEffects.Add/Remove) did not appear in the top 60: it is event-driven on build/toggle, not per tick. Real share about 3.5% of the tick, all in per-character application (about 2.4 effects per character, one ContinuousEffect object per effect per tick).
per_window.power: BatteryService.Tick, MechanicalGraph*, MechanicalNode* did not appear in the top 60; counters are event-driven (OnNodePower*Changed) and PowerEfficiency is a division over cached sums (6,840 reads per tick, about 0.6%). No per-tick recomputation on supply changes.

records.conclusion: None of the three areas has an exact-preserving change above about 1-2%: power is already event-driven; area effects apply per character (small allocations, string-keyed need lookup) and their wide-area coverage is maintained on events; pathfinding is a heap A* whose time is mostly cached flow-field queries from behaviors (about 2000 per tick) and path-corner transforms. Candidates of about 1% each: inline need predicates in NeedManager.UpdateNeed, avoid the per-tick GetComponent/allocations in RangedEffectSubject.ApplyEffects, single neighbor scan in FlowFieldPathBuilder.AddEdgeNode.
limits: Whole-class hooking inflates inclusive times of tiny methods (0.1-0.3 us rows are mostly hook overhead).
Single window; counts per tick are representative, absolute times are not.

coarse_mode.summary: -t3mpTestMovementCoarse: advance corner to corner in one MoveToward() step (MoveInDirection without MaxMovementStep) unless the segment's closest point to the path end lies inside the stopping proximity (SegmentTouchesEnd, a superset of the native 0.1-unit grid check); such segments keep native 0.1-unit stepping, so the stop rule and provider call positions/counts stay native. Changes low-order position bits and the number of animated corners.
coarse_mode.trial_copy: testlogs/movement-substeps-20260915/Code-coarse-v2.dll (review fixes; Code-coarse.dll is the first coarse build A02A258A used for the first audit and the first two pairs)

audit.index_diff_details: all three: corner index off by one at a corner arrival, positions (102.500015 vs 102.499565), (237.4996 vs 237.5), (136.502014 vs 136.5)

Together with the bit-exact mode's +3% this is the first single change in the series that reaches the +9% needed for 1.5x on n10c. Absolute values vary with the machine's interactive use.
limits: Not bit-exact with vanilla: positions differ in low-order bits (max 0.002 units in the audits); a corner arrival and its provider call can shift by one tick at tick edges (2-3 per 520,000 calls in the audits). Arrival state at the path end matched in every audited call.
Audits restart from native state on every call, so they bound per-call divergence, not cumulative drift over a long session.
Three valid pairs at x50 and two at x7, all on a machine in interactive use; re-measure idle before adoption.
No 6-scenario or visual play test; other mods that depend on 0.1-unit intermediate corners or per-sub-step MoveInDirection calls would see fewer calls.

coarse_mode.review: gpt-6-astra high read-only (testlogs/codex/movement-coarse-review-20260915.md): P1 SegmentTouchesEnd was not a strict superset of native stepping because native sub-step positions drift off the exact segment by rounding (float32 reproduction: grazing case inside for native, outside for the closest point); fixed by pulling the closest point 0.01 units toward the path end before the proximity test (TouchMargin). P2 the audit tolerance also accepted transform round-trip/restoration failures; fixed with a separate integrityFailures counter that the script never tolerates. P2 (accepted, documented): dropping intermediate steps skips the native RemainingTimeThreshold/RemainingDistanceThreshold decisions between 0.1-unit steps, so at tick edges (remaining time within about 1e-4 s of a step boundary) a corner arrival and its provider call can shift by one tick; this is part of the accepted non-exactness, not rounding. MoveToward, state, fallback, mirror/restoration and script routing were found correct.

records.question: Can managed transition-entry guards make activeInHierarchy notification caching safe without thinning simulation?
records.conditions: Steam 1.1.2.4 / Unity Mono. n10c loaded as paused host; only independent synthetic objects were cached and observed. No gameplay entity lookup was replaced. Every shadow read returned the native value.
records.design: Two policies, ten scenarios each. Both guard SetActive, SetParent, Destroy and DestroyImmediate with entry invalidation and in-flight native fallback. Policy 2 also marks scheduled-destroy descendants uncacheable and guards AnimationClip.SampleAnimation. Invalidation is scoped to tracked synthetic objects to prevent unrelated UI activity masking the test. Reader-before-observer callback order and guard entry counts are recorded; expected counts are asserted.

results.notification_only_negative_controls: 2 stale reads in each policy; guards disabled for these controls.
results.managed_transition_cases: Self, previously warmed caller, parent activation, reparent, nested callbacks, immediate destruction and zero-delay destruction: zero mismatches under both policies. Zero-delay destruction callback occurred inside the guard; this does not validate arbitrary delayed lifetimes.
results.explicit_animation_sampling: Policy 1: one stale read, zero guard entries. Policy 2: zero stale reads, one guard entry.
results.automatic_animation_playback: One stale read in each policy, zero guard entries, reader before observer. The native Animation player changes m_IsActive without entering the guarded managed APIs.

records.decision: Do not integrate this managed-transition cache into v1.2.1. Adding the explicit sampler hook repairs that call path but does not cover automatic native animation playback. No TPS/FPS A/B was run because correctness did not pass.
records.limits: A synthetic callback-order counterexample, not an n10c gameplay bug reproduction or proof that all future lookup optimizations are impossible. Hierarchies excluded from caching and other native lifecycle paths have not been evaluated. The first exploratory run used global invalidation and could mask deferred comparisons; it is not acceptance evidence.

records.question: What produces the v1.1.7 versus v1.2.1 speed gap, separately from which feature is largest inside legacy?
records.conditions: n10c / Steam 1.1.2.4 / same camera and graphics / matched effective speed / Shift+O and blackout OFF / fresh process per arm. Ten runs at x50 (warmup 256, measured 1024 ticks); ten at x7 (warmup 64, measured 512 ticks). FPS at x7 because TPS is speed-limited. Compare only within each speed/window.

design.All: Original legacy binary; all measured features on.
design.NoMirror: Legacy with activeInHierarchy mirror and sentinel template injection off; flat dispatch and OldExtras on.
design.OldExtras: Legacy with nine additional groups (37 flags) off; flat dispatch and Unity active-state mirror on.
design.OldExtrasNoMirror: Union of OldExtras and NoMirror (39 flags off); flat dispatch remains on.
design.Current: Installed v1.2.1; Frontier, event delegates, water-upload deduplication, walking delegate reuse, terrain visit optimization and tube fix. No experimental tick-port code.
design.order: All, Current, OldExtras, OldExtrasNoMirror, NoMirror; then the reverse sequence. Two observations of each arm per speed.

records.variant_definition: Use scripts/LegacyVariants/groups.json for All, NoMirror and OldExtras. OldExtrasNoMirror is the deduplicated union of the latter two. scripts/LegacyVariants changes only audited true-to-false initializer bytes in a copy of the actual Workshop DLL; verify SHA256 and exact live settings, not retained MVID alone.
conclusions: Legacy is faster than current in both measured conditions. This confirms throughput/FPS, not identical simulation decisions or game outcomes.

Keeping legacy flat dispatch but removing both Unity active-state tracking and the nine additional groups makes legacy slower than current in both conditions. These two feature sets together create the legacy advantage over this current configuration; flat dispatch alone does not explain the version gap.

Both feature sets have positive measured conditional effects with the other set on or off. Their percentages have different denominators and contexts; do not sum them or assign unique shares of the version gap.

Current Frontier already eliminates visits to entities with no enabled tickables, then uses native entity/component execution. Legacy flat dispatch uses consolidated arrays and Enabled bits, and optionally the Unity active-state mirror. They reduce some of the same dispatch work through different implementations.

The historical 13.4% flat contrast was NoMirror versus NoFlat within legacy, with active-state tracking off in both. It also changes Enabled-bit dispatch and per-entity cached-entry traversal; it was not a measured 13.4% addition to current Frontier.

OldExtras includes frame-based haul decision reuse and every-other-call district resource counting. Other groups include legitimate optimizations or overhead; the aggregate benefit does not mean every member is beneficial or safe to port.

Why the versions differ is now tested at these two interacting feature-set boundaries. A safe implementation that closes the gap, unique per-feature shares of the total gap, and whole-save outcome equivalence are not established by this experiment.

code_audit.flat_dispatch: BucketSnapshot.Components/EnabledBits/Starts; TryTickAll flat branch, source lines 30671-30795. NoFlat arm also removes EnabledBits use and restores per-entity cached-entry iteration/live BaseComponent.Enabled. Thus the historical 13.4% contrast includes this machinery, not only elimination of method calls.
code_audit.unity_active_lookup: ActiveInHierarchySentinel.OnEnable/OnDisable publishes active bits (30201-30228); normal flat branch reads bit or native activeInHierarchy if no slot (30733-30748).
code_audit.current_frontier: src/T3MP/Runtime/TickFrontier.cs: NeedsVisit/NextIndex tracks nonempty entity groups; normal TickAllFast calls native entity.Tick. Actual installed 86AD source paths exclude all TICK_PORT_EXPERIMENT branches.
code_audit.haul: HaulNoActionFrameCache uses Time.frameCount and skips repeated no-action workplace Decide in that frame (15989-16023).
code_audit.district: DistrictResourceCounterThrottle increments a per-instance call count and executes only each second call (11527-11543). It is not a frame-key cache.
code_audit.interpretation_limit: Legacy timings measure actual tick/FPS throughput, not equal behavior decisions or equal game state outputs. OldExtras is 37 disabled flags in nine groups, not one feature or 37 independent measured contributions.

validation.live_checks: Every result passed identity, expected flags, effective speed, graphics, focus, origin and completed tick checks. Post-analysis additionally compares game, source, driver, exact tick interval and display across separate invocations. All 20 must match within their speed cohort.
validation.review: gpt-6-astra high read-only review. Initial outer-runner default and cross-invocation condition-check findings corrected; retroactive post-analysis verifies the already-running x50 block, and the corrected outer runner additionally guards x7. Final review: None.

limits: Two observations per arm; point estimates are not confidence intervals. Large order relationships repeat; do not force fine ranking of close values.

NoMirror changes both lookup and its sentinel injection. OldExtras is a bundle of nine groups, not one optimization. Current differs in additional runtime/loading implementation details, so OldExtrasNoMirror versus Current is not an isolated flat-versus-Frontier microbenchmark.
Legacy frame caches can change workload and behavior. Higher TPS does not prove the same decisions were executed.
Continuous play only; placement/selection UI and load time are not ranked here. Resource sampling every five seconds gives approximate external-load alignment.
records.restoration: Original current DLL, Workshop DLL and source save verified unchanged; mod preferences restored; test driver removed. No product code changes, commit, push or Workshop upload in this investigation.

records.implementation: Consolidated ordered component arrays per bucket, exact Enabled setter tracking, existing Frontier eligibility index retained. Preserve live sorted membership, execution order, native Unity activeInHierarchy reads, metrics and exception scope. Disable new dispatch and Frontier skipping on guarded call-chain regeneration.
records.conditions: n10c / Steam 1.1.2.4 / D3D11 / matched graphics, camera and effective speed / Shift+O off / fresh process per arm. Equal tick windows and driver within each cohort. Final artifact high-load BPPB follows prototype high-load BPPB and normal-speed PBBP.

prototype.limit: Precedes final native fallback bridge and observer-order compatibility corrections. Normal x7 adjacent comparisons reverse; no confirmed normal FPS gain. Prototype results do not identify the final product artifact.

records.interpretation: Final high-load mean is 0.69% below 86AD; adjacent pair directions reverse. Stable improvement is unconfirmed. The earlier prototype gain was not reproduced by the final artifact. Normal builds exclude the trial. The legacy flat-dispatch 13.4% contribution is not a prediction of incremental improvement over current Frontier; no new vanilla-relative multiplier is established.

records.method: Legacy variants change only constant-true BenchmarkSettings initializer bytes to false. Every changed byte, loaded settings, module identity, mode, timing interval and restoration checked. MVID is retained; SHA256 plus live settings distinguish variants. records.groups: Exact disabled settings: scripts/LegacyVariants/groups.json. NoMirror disables active-state mirror and sentinel injection. NoFlat additionally disables flat dispatch; per-entity legacy dispatch remains. OldExtras disables the nine measured groups other than Tick and Events, including the old walking-delegate implementation. LoadVisuals disables PreparedEntityVisuals with its CLI flag; all runtime settings stay ON.
limits: These are legacy counterfactual performance measurements, not proof of equivalent simulation work or safe portability. Frame caches can change decisions and workload.
Single-feature effects depend on the other enabled features. Do not add them or assign unique shares of the version gap; OldExtras measures the combined effect directly.
All vs NoFlat includes both flat dispatch and active-state tracking. Compare NoMirror vs NoFlat for flat dispatch with the mirror disabled in both.
Normal speed uses FPS because TPS reaches the requested-speed ceiling. Small effects with one sample are screening results, not a reliable fine ranking.
The two speeds use different fixed tick windows (65-577 and 257-1281). Comparisons within each speed are matched; differences between speeds cannot be attributed to speed alone.
No runtime code was ported or deployed by this investigation. Original current DLL, Workshop DLL, save and mod preferences restored/verified.

The second speed-7 NoMirror sample had higher external CPU load (0.867 cores versus 0.355 in the first). Both were slower than the bracketing all-ON controls; do not overstate the precise FPS percentage.
records.reproduce: Build scripts/LegacyVariants from the audited original DLL into an ignored directory; build T3MPTestDriver; use run_fixed_tick_ab.ps1 -MatchedConditions -Order P -ExpectedExperiment LegacyRuntime -ComparisonDll <variant.dll> -LegacyVariantRecord <variants.json>. All/Current controls use P-All/B. Add -LegacyVisualPreparationBaseline for isolated P-All load-visual control.
conclusions: Legacy tick dispatch is the largest measured legacy runtime contributor. Its flat component dispatch and activeInHierarchy mirror both contribute; current v1.2.1 uses Frontier instead.

At speed 50, pooled TPS: current 19.165290, legacy 21.496469, legacy with the nine OldExtras groups disabled 19.690713. At speed 7, pooled FPS: 13.251595, 14.879878 and 13.685864 respectively. Removing the combined extras substantially narrows the version gap; the residual is not a pure tick-implementation measurement.

Haul no-action caching gives a repeated speed-50 contribution; its speed-7 FPS contribution was not established. Navigation/events show small screening differences. Harvest, needs, water, district, worker and visual groups did not establish a large individual gain.
PreparedEntityVisuals OFF did not show a material steady-state TPS/FPS loss in this test. This does not assess placement/selection response.

The evidence supports investigating tick dispatch and active-state lookup with current behavior/compatibility preserved. Legacy result caches and whole-method replacement are not approved for reintroduction by these timings.

records.method: Each speed: three all-on reference runs and two runs per disabled feature in reverse order. Matched effective speed, camera, graphics and simulation tick interval. x7 uses FPS because TPS is speed-limited; x50 uses TPS. For the descriptive point estimate, interpolate the bracketing all-on references by measurement midpoint and compute all_on/off - 1; combine the two ratios geometrically. This assumes smooth reference drift and is not a confidence interval. Bracketing baseline values and each raw OFF result are retained for sensitivity checks.
records.interpretation: Frontier is the clear largest contributor in both conditions. Event delegates and water uploads form the next candidate tier, especially for normal-speed FPS; their fine ordering is uncertain. Walker delegates and terrain visits have no established standalone throughput gain here. Tiny positive or negative estimates must not be interpreted as proof of benefit or harm.
limits: Two samples per disabled feature; all-on references themselves vary, especially x7. No forced ranking of overlapping small effects.
These are marginal effects in the current combination, not independent shares of the total mod gain; do not add percentages or multiply factors.
Scope is this save and fixed post-load tick window, not a guarantee for other maps, populations, camera positions or longer steady-state play.
Scene load times are ancillary observations under the common visual-preparation control, not a ranking of all load optimizations.
External CPU sampled every five seconds; timed-window alignment is approximate. No unrelated process was stopped.

records.summary: Where n10c2 (larger population) spends tick time with v1.2.3, and which items admit an output-identical rewrite. Sources: tick profile testlogs/tick-profile-n10c2-20260916-014013 (window 4, 250 ticks, profiler-inflated), hot counts testlogs/hot-counts-n10c2-20260916-024709 (400-tick windows), subsystem profile testlogs/subsystem-profile-n10c2-20260916-025043 (400-tick windows; per-call hook overhead ~0.2-0.3 us inflates every count-heavy item).
records.baseline: no-mod 13.575 vs v1.2.3 20.792 ticks/s at x50 (1.532x, n10c2-baseline-20260916); median frame 2.4 s with the mod, 3.7 s without.

hot_counts_per_tick.StorableGoodRegistry.GetAmount: 10.3k (n10c: 7.6k before AllowedGoodRows); callers other than the fill calculator remain unattributed

items.cost: 1.59 s inclusive per 250 ticks in the tick profile (~6 ms/tick profiled); ActionDurationCalculator.DurationWithReturnInHours 454k calls/250 ticks = ~1.8k/tick, each two cached flow-field queries (FindPathUnlimitedRange ~1.2-3 us) plus Walker.CalculateTravelTimeInHours
items.algorithm: for each appraised group (by points) iterate every need behavior (building) computing travel(current->action)+travel(action->return)+0.3h and keep the strict minimum; first group with a feasible action wins
items.exact_option: prune a candidate before its two path queries when a valid lower bound of its duration is >= the current best (strict '<' means it could never win; feasibility check is per candidate). The bound must account for node snapping: two positions in one cell give path distance 0 while their Euclidean distance is up to ~1.4, so a plain Euclidean bound is NOT valid. Needs NavigationService's snapping/heuristic rules (HeuristicDistance is used when no path exists) to derive distance >= euclid - snap slack, converted with the walker's base speed and the same SecondsToHours arithmetic. Estimated gain 2-4% if most far candidates prune; unimplemented.
items.risk: a wrong bound changes decisions; validate with a replay audit in the driver (compare pruned decision with the unpruned minimum for every call) before any A/B

items.algorithm: every hauler decision walks all haul candidates in the district, each provider computes weights from input/output fill percentages, then List.Sort by weight (introsort, unstable: any replacement must call the same sort)
items.exact_option: none without caching across ticks (forbidden). Fill percentages already use AllowedGoodRows. Only micro-work left (allocation of WeightedBehavior structs is free). Not worth a trial.

items.algorithm: rebuilds stock and capacity dictionaries from all district inventories each tick: per inventory Stock enumeration, Gives() = OutputGoods.Contains, dictionary ContainsKey+indexer per good
items.exact_option: output-identical micro rewrite (single TryGetValue instead of ContainsKey+two indexer calls; GetCapacity already optimized). Expected <1%. Event-driven incremental counting would be a logic change (ordering of updates within a tick) and is not proposed.

items.algorithm: GetStalest rotates the dwelling list until one has a free slot, then scans the district population (LINQ Concat of adults/children) calling GetComponent<Dweller>, IsLookingForBetterHome, CanAssignDweller (GetComponent<Child> inside) until one moves in; with no mover the whole population is scanned every tick
items.exact_option: the per-beaver cost is component lookups; an exact rewrite could only cache Dweller/Child components per Beaver (ConditionalWeakTable) - allowed (identity, not state) but small; expected ~1%. Low priority.

items.cost: still the largest component share; profiled 49.5% is inflated by the profiler's fallback (hooks on PathFollower helpers)
items.exact_option: already replaced (MovementSubsteps); no further exact idea

records.conclusion: One algorithmic candidate remains on n10c2 with a plausible 2-4%: lower-bound pruning in PickShortestAction, conditional on a provably valid distance bound under node snapping. Everything else is <1% or requires caching/decision changes the user has excluded.
